rows.boundary: Vitruvius gives the eye’s one-part diameter, its unequal position in an eight-part height, and a half-eye reduction in quadrant operations. He does not state eight quarter turns or locate the complete set of compass centres. This drawing continues the half-eye decrement through eight quarters about one fixed eye centre: a modern two-turn schematic with linear-radius interpolation and a chosen fillet. It is not a recovered compass construction. The promised ancient figure is not preserved here; how far in from the abacus edge the eye sits is also disputed.
rows.finalJoin: The two radius directions differ by 8.130102°. Their tangents turn by the same angle.
